page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture uses the x86_64 instruction set with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 33 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptography instructions including AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, providing a standard balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, requiring persistent network-attached block storage for operating system and data requirements.

Benchmark results place the n2-standard-32 consistently in the middle 50% across general compute and memory tests. In CPU workloads, it achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1175.0, a multi-core score of 9858.0, and a PassMark CPU mark of 27193.8. Synthetic stress testing registers 1837.79 on single-core stress-ng and 30011.12 on multi-core runs. Memory subsystem testing shows large-block uncached read throughput of 166.42 GB/sec and write speeds of 85.05 GB/sec, while cached read speeds reach 1654.01 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression settles in the bottom 25% at 23.79 GB/sec, reflecting moderate per-thread instruction throughput.

Operational performance metrics validate the system for intermediate and backend processing roles. The instance manages 26.98 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves static web serving throughput of 21.35 GB/sec. Software compilation via Clang reaches 21814.0 in Geekbench subtests. While CPU-based LLM inference handles small 135M parameter models at 81.34 tokens per second and 7B models at 12.42 tokens per second, large 70B prompt processing drops to 4.16 tokens per second in the bottom 10%, indicating that heavier neural network tasks are inefficient on this CPU-only profile.

Qualitatively, the n2-standard-32 provides balanced resource density for enterprise compute workloads without paying premiums for specialized hardware accelerators. Workloads best suited for this instance include medium-to-large relational databases, distributed caching nodes, CI/CD compilation runners, batch data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving infrastructure.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-32 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz and 128.0 GB of memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Built on the x86_64 architecture with 16 physical cores, hyperthreading, and AVX-512 vector support, it includes no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show solid mid-tier performance across varied multi-core workloads, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 9858.0, a PassMark CPU score of 27193.8, and 26.98 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput remains steady with 166.42 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads. While single-threaded compression and large-scale LLM execution demonstrate lower relative throughput, the system offers predictable computational density. The configuration is appropriate for distributed web servers, software build pipelines, batch data processing, and in-memory caching layers.
